name: Yong
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD diss., Cornell (only ref Glottolog cites; includes Yong data) — Yong-specific phonology otherwise in Thai-language theses, not located online

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x, languoid yong1277 'Yong' and reference records 17319 (Pittayaporn 2009), 119851 (Pittayaporn 2009 JSEALS), 701778 (Ethnologue 28).
sources.note: Bibliography only: Piyawat (Wangsai) 2007 Kasetsart MA (phonology, Thai, 279 pp.), Deephungton 1987 (grammar sketch, French, 444 pp.), Pittayaporn 2009.

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University.
sources.note: Yong mentioned only in the classification note 'Tai Yong is a dialect of Lue' (the text); the stress discussion concerns Proto-Tai word shape (sesquisyllables), not Yong. Not a Yong description.

sources.citation: Pornsawan Ploykaew. 1985. The phonology of Lue in Chiangrai Province. MA thesis, Mahidol University (held under luuu1242, sister Lue check).
sources.note: Per the luuu1242 summary: p. 46 'Strong stress.. always occurs on a monosyllabic word and on the final syllable of any polysyllabic word.. it is non-phonemic'. This is Lue of Mae Suai (Chiang Rai), not Yong; noted only because Yong is classified as a Lue dialect (Pittayaporn 2009).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Yong language' (en) and 'ภาษายอง' (th), raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Six tones (from Intajamornrak 2019); nothing on stress; Thai page cites Wangsai 2007.

sources.citation: ปิยาภรณ์ ไชยพันธุ์ (Piyaporn Chaiyaphan). 2567 [2024]. การแปรศัพท์ภาษายอง จังหวัดลำพูน ตามตัวแปรอายุ = Lexical variation of Yong language spoken in Lamphun province by three age groups. MA thesis (Linguistics), Mahidol University, 165 pp. Handle 123456789/91847.
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 2.4 'ระบบเสียงภาษายอง' (pp. 23-26) is a second-hand summary of Yong phonology from Niamnak 1985, Pankhuenkhat 1978, Wangsai 2007 and Soiyana 2009: 21 initials, 9 finals, 18 monophthongs, 6 tones (A12-34, B/C/DL/DS 123-4). The only occurrence of การเน้นเสียง (p. 26) summarises Khanthawong 2010: speech rate and emphasis cause syllable deletion/addition. Full Thai bibliography of Yong phonology work on pp. 124-197.

sources.citation: Intajamornrak, Chommanad. 2019. Tonal variation caused by language contact: a case study of the Yong language. 13th ICLEHI 2019 Osaka, paper 013-012, 9 pp. (Naresuan University).
sources.note: Nothing. Acoustic study of the six Yong tones (Pa Bong Luang, Mae Chan, Chiang Rai; three age groups); 'stress'/'accent' do not occur; only checked vs non-checked syllables. Its reference list names the Yong phonology theses (Neamnark 1985, Pankhuenkhat 1988, Wangsai 2007).

sources.citation: Hartmann, John F. 2008. The Lue language. In Diller, Edmondson & Luo (eds), The Tai-Kadai languages, 254-297. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Nothing on stress in ch. 7 (a full-text search for stress/accent the whole chapter). Discusses Lue of Moeng Yong (Gedney 1969 notes) and Yong of Chiang Mai (Davies 1979) for tone splits; 7.2 Phonology: 'the Tai languages being basically monosyllabic.. the syllable is the unit of tone placement'. Bibliography gives Davies, Somchit 1979 'A comparative study of Yong and Standard Thai', in Theraphan L-Thongkum et al. (eds), 26-48.

sources.citation: ดิศราพร สร้อยญาณะ (Disaraporn Soiyana). 2552 [2009]. การศึกษาวรรณยุกต์ภาษายองเชิงกลสัทศาสตร์: การเปรียบเทียบในบริบทคำพูดเดี่ยวกับคำพูดต่อเนื่องและระหว่างสองรุ่นอายุ [An acoustic study of Yong tones: citation vs connected speech and two generations]. MA thesis (Linguistics), Chulalongkorn University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Instrumental tone study contrasting citation forms with connected speech; the connected-speech condition is where stress/prominence effects on tone would be described.

sources.citation: วิสุทธิระ เนียมนาค (Wisuthira Niamnak; cited in English as W. Neamnark). 2528 [1985]. ระบบเสียงภาษายองซึ่งพูดในจังหวัดลำพูน: การศึกษาเปรียบเทียบแบบร่วมสมัย [Lamphun Yong phonology: a synchronic comparative study]. MA thesis (Linguistics), Chulalongkorn University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The primary phonological description of Lamphun Yong, the base of all later work (Chaiyaphan 2024 adopts its consonant system); a Chula linguistics MA of this era normally has a chapter on syllable/word structure where a stress statement would appear (cf. Ploykaew 1985 for Lue).
